entries.title: Matthew 11:2
segments: In the prison. At Machaerus, a fortified place about five miles east of the Dead Sea.

entries.title: Matthew 11:3
segments: He that cometh. The Messiah.  Perhaps it was not John himself who was doubtful but his disciples, and he wished them to know that Jesus was really the Messiah.  Or through his disappointment he may have come to have doubts.

entries.title: Matthew 11:6
segments: Blessed is he, etc.  Blessed is he who clearly sees in these miracles proofs that I am the Messiah.

entries.title: Matthew 11:7
segments: What went ye out into the wilderness to behold? Jesus defends John in
from any reproach of luxury or of weakness of faith and character, yet in the last clause of

he that is but little in the kingdom of heaven is declared to be greater than the Baptist.  This refers to the new order or dispensation brought in by Jesus himself.  In that order the least surpassed the greatest in the old.

entries.title: Matthew 11:12
segments: Suffereth violence. The most eager and sincere pursuit of righteousness wins the highest reward in the spiritual life.  This truth was strikingly illustrated by the aggressive enthusiasm of John as the herald of the kingdom of heaven.  Such men take the kingdom, as it were, by force.

entries.title: Matthew 11:16
segments: Like unto children. By this comparison with children playing games is meant that the Jews were too frivolous and insincere to take either Jesus or John seriously.

entries.title: Matthew 11:19
segments: Wisdom. The truths announced by Jesus and John.

entries.title: Matthew 11:21
segments:
Chorazin. Two and a half miles north of Tell Hum (Capernaum) on the coast of the Sea of Galilee.  It has been identified with the modern Kerazeh.
 

 
Bethsaida. Near the northern extremity of the Sea of Galilee.  The five thousand were fed there.
 

 
Tyre and Sidon. Phoenician cities on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.

entries.title: Matthew 11:25
segments:
Father. Jesus in this prayer of thanksgiving and worship addresses God as Father before ascribing to Him the sovereignty of heaven and earth.
 

 
From the wise and understanding. The simple tidings of Christ's message were hidden from the proud and self-sufficient Pharisees and scribes, but they were revealed to babes, that is, to the humble and unlearned who received them gladly.

entries.title: Matthew 11:27
segments:
All things have been delivered unto me. Jesus, who prayed to God as Father and Lord of heaven and earth, now affirms that he has equal authority with the Father.
 

 
No one knoweth the Son, save the Father. The person and office of the Son are not to be understood in their fullness by man.
 

 
He to whomsoever the Son willeth. Jesus not only knows the Father as no one else can know Him, but he alone can make known the Father.  Only Jesus Christ can reveal God to man.

entries.title: Matthew 11:28
segments: Come unto me. Having declared that he alone can reveal the Father, Jesus freely invites all who find life to be a struggle and a burden to test his power and willingness to give rest and peace.

entries.title: Matthew 11:29
segments:
My yoke. My commands; the self-denials necessary as my followers.
 

 
I am meek and lowly in heart. Jesus thus makes himself the divine example of the humility necessary in learning about God.

entries.title: Matthew 11:30
segments: My burden. Self-surrender to Christ, whatever sufferings may result, is a light burden compared with the heavy penalties of sin.
